extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public, organizations, or representatives seeking to propose or comment on OATH rules (petitioners, regulated parties, attorneys, advocacy groups)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for proposing, submitting, and tracking rulemaking at the NYC Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH): explains OATH's CAPA-based obligations, how to file a new rule petition, how proposed/final rules are published, and how the public can comment or attend hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the City Administrative Procedure Act (CAPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: OATH proposes and adopts rules in accordance with the City Administrative Procedure Act (CAPA). OATH publishes its proposed and final rules in The City Record and NYC Rules. OATH holds public hearings and accepts comments from the public on proposed rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the procedural framework OATH must follow: publication for notice, opportunities for public comment, and conducting hearings as required by CAPA. The page points users to where proposed and final rules appear (The City Record, NYC Rules) so they can monitor notices and participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Rule Petition required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: If you would like to propose a new rule to OATH, you can submit a typewritten petition. The petition should include: the proposed rule and all suggested language of the rule that you would like OATH to consider; your argument in support of the rule; you or your authorized representative’s name, telephone number, mailing address, and email address; and your or your authorized representative’s signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be typewritten and must include full proposed rule text plus a supporting argument and contact information for the petitioner or authorized representative. Inclusion of signature is required. This is the minimum content OATH expects when considering a petition to adopt a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to submit a rule petition
rubrics_metrics.description: OATH accepts petition submissions by email, mail, or in-person delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email: Rules_Oath@oath.nyc.gov. Mail or In-Person: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings, 66 John Street, 11th Floor, New York, NY 10038, ATTN: General Counsel. Use these channels to file the required typewritten petition and supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication venues for proposed and final rules
rubrics_metrics.description: OATH publishes its proposed and final rules in The City Record and NYC Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners and commenters should monitor The City Record and NYC Rules for notices, proposed rule text, and final rule adoptions. Publication in these venues is part of CAPA notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearings and acceptance of written comments
rubrics_metrics.description: OATH holds public hearings and accepts comments from the public on proposed rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each proposed rule, OATH typically makes available a public hearing (with transcript) and invites written comments. The page links to transcripts of hearings and written comments for specific rulemakings, indicating that hearings are recorded and comments are part of the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for submission and processing of rulemaking petitions (procedural rules exist)
rubrics_metrics.description: OATH has rules for submission and processing of rulemaking petitions and provides links for more information about current Proposed Rules and recent Final Rules, and on how to attend a public hearing and submit a comment on a proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedural requirements (deadlines, formatting, processing steps) are covered in the referenced 'Rules for Submission and Processing of Rulemaking Petitions' and linked pages; prospective petitioners should consult those links for step-by-step instructions beyond the basic required contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/examples of matters that may be addressed by OATH rules
rubrics_metrics.description: OATH's rulemaking can amend Rules of Practice, penalty schedules, procedures for appearances and representation, processes for reopening defaults and requesting new hearings, cross-references to other agencies' rules, processes to petition agencies, procedures for remote proceedings, settlement negotiation procedures, and administrative procedures such as amending judgments to correct legal names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists numerous recent proposed and final rules and hearing transcripts as concrete examples of permissible subjects and typical amendments. Use these examples to gauge whether a proposed petition falls within OATH's regulatory domain and typical scope of rule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal research resources for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: OATH provides references and links useful for rulemaking and research: NYC Charter Chapter Establishing OATH, Glossary of legal terms, BenchNOTES, New York City Rules, American Legal Publishing Corporation, NYC Administrative Law Online Library (database of decisions, orders, opinions), The City Record, New York City Council Legislation, Laws of New York State, ACRIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources are recommended for drafting petitions, researching existing rules and legal context, checking statutory or charter authority, and assembling supporting legal arguments or citations.
